_doc: Infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations, each stated as a control that public hardening benchmarks define, then instantiated in the formats a project actually ships. Control TEXT is third-party — these are the checks every published cloud/container hardening baseline agrees on — while the snippets are minimal instantiations written here, because no benchmark ships code.
_pairs: Every control has a `vulnerable` and a `hardened` variant, and scoring is VERDICT-FLIP, not detection count: the vulnerable one must fire and the hardened one must not. A detector that reports both is not detecting the control, it is reporting the resource — and that failure is invisible to a recall-only bench. Same doctrine as bench/mutation.
_endToEnd: The runner scans a real directory through the shipped scan path rather than calling detectors directly. Admission is where IaC support has actually failed before: `k8s-admission` was fully implemented, wired and unit-tested while returning zero through a scan, because the file never reached the walker.

controls.control: Security groups must not allow unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to administrative ports
Object storage buckets must not grant public read access
Managed database instances must have encryption at rest enabled
IAM policies must not grant Action "*" on Resource "*"
Containers must not run in privileged mode
controls.vulnerable:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/app:1.0.0
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
controls.hardened:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/app:1.0.0
          securityContext:
            privileged: false
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false

controls.control: Pods must not share the host network namespace
controls.vulnerable:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: registry.example.com/api:2.1.0
controls.hardened:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  hostNetwork: false
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: registry.example.com/api:2.1.0

controls.control: Containers must not run as the root user
controls.vulnerable:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: worker
spec:
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: registry.example.com/worker:1.0.0
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 0
controls.hardened:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: worker
spec:
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: registry.example.com/worker:1.0.0
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001

controls.control: Credentials must not be supplied as literal environment values in a manifest
controls.vulnerable:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: registry.example.com/app:1.0.0
      env:
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          value: "Kd8fJ2mQx9Lp4Zt1"
controls.hardened:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: registry.example.com/app:1.0.0
      env:
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: app-secrets
              key: db-password

controls.control: Security groups must not allow unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to administrative ports
controls.vulnerable:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  WebSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: web
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
controls.hardened:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  WebSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: web
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/8

controls.control: Object storage buckets must not grant public read access
controls.vulnerable:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  AssetsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      AccessControl: PublicRead
controls.hardened:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  AssetsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      AccessControl: Private
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true

controls.control: Blob storage containers must not allow anonymous public access
Chart values must not default a workload to privileged execution
controls.vulnerable:
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/app
  tag: "1.0.0"
securityContext:
  privileged: true
  runAsUser: 0
controls.hardened:
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/app
  tag: "1.0.0"
securityContext:
  privileged: false
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 10001

controls.control: Container images must not run as root
controls.vulnerable:
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
USER root
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
controls.hardened:
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
USER app
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

controls.control: Base images must be pinned to an immutable reference
controls.vulnerable:
FROM ubuntu:latest
RUN addgroup --system app && adduser --system --ingroup app app
USER app
CMD ["/bin/sh"]
controls.hardened:
FROM ubuntu@sha256:5e5f6f0a2ea0c9e6e2e6b1e33b8b1e0c8a9d3f2e1b0a9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f
RUN addgroup --system app && adduser --system --ingroup app app
USER app
CMD ["/bin/sh"]
controls.note: Moved from `build/Dockerfile`. `build/` is in the walker's DEFAULT_IGNORE list as build OUTPUT, so a Dockerfile kept there is never scanned — a real limitation, recorded in the README rather than fixed here, because changing DEFAULT_IGNORE affects every scan and `build/` genuinely is an output directory for several toolchains.

metadata:

spec:

  containers:
    - name: agent

controls.hardened:

controls.control: Containers must not add dangerous Linux capabilities
controls.vulnerable:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: net
spec:
  containers:
    - name: net
      image: registry.example.com/net:1.0.0
      securityContext:
        capabilities:
          add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]
controls.hardened:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: net
spec:
  containers:
    - name: net
      image: registry.example.com/net:1.0.0
      securityContext:
        capabilities:
          drop: ["ALL"]

controls.control: Managed databases must not be publicly accessible
controls.vulnerable:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  Database:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      Engine: postgres
      PubliclyAccessible: true
      StorageEncrypted: true
controls.hardened:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  Database:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      Engine: postgres
      PubliclyAccessible: false
      StorageEncrypted: true

controls.control: IAM policies must not grant Action "*" on Resource "*"
controls.vulnerable:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  AdminPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: '*'
            Resource: '*'
controls.hardened:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  AdminPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: ['s3:GetObject']
            Resource: 'arn:aws:s3:::assets/*'

controls.control: Network security rules must not allow inbound from any source to administrative ports
Chart values must not default a workload onto the host network
controls.vulnerable:
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/api
  tag: "2.0.0"
hostNetwork: true
controls.hardened:
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/api
  tag: "2.0.0"
hostNetwork: false

controls.control: Remote content must not be fetched with ADD
controls.vulnerable:
FROM ubuntu@sha256:5e5f6f0a2ea0c9e6e2e6b1e33b8b1e0c8a9d3f2e1b0a9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f
ADD https://example.com/installer.sh /tmp/installer.sh
RUN addgroup --system app && adduser --system --ingroup app app
USER app
controls.hardened:
FROM ubuntu@sha256:5e5f6f0a2ea0c9e6e2e6b1e33b8b1e0c8a9d3f2e1b0a9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f
COPY installer.sh /tmp/installer.sh
RUN addgroup --system app && adduser --system --ingroup app app
USER app

controls.control: Block storage volumes must be encrypted at rest

controls.why: wildcard-EQUIVALENT with no literal Action "*" — needs the rule to reason about what the actions add up to, not to match a character
controls.control: IAM policies must not grant effectively unrestricted privilege

controls.why: the open CIDR arrives through a Parameter default — the literal never appears on the ingress rule, which is the indirection iac-terraform.js resolves for HCL and nothing resolves for CloudFormation
controls.control: Security groups must not allow unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to administrative ports
controls.vulnerable:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Parameters:
  AllowedCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 0.0.0.0/0
Resources:
  WebSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: web
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref AllowedCidr
controls.hardened:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Parameters:
  AllowedCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.0.0/8
Resources:
  WebSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: web
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: !Ref AllowedCidr

controls.why: an ABSENCE, not a pattern — a container with no resources.limits can starve every other pod on the node, and there is no string to match
controls.control: Containers must declare CPU and memory limits
controls.vulnerable:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: batch
spec:
  containers:
    - name: batch
      image: registry.example.com/batch:1.0.0
controls.hardened:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: batch
spec:
  containers:
    - name: batch
      image: registry.example.com/batch:1.0.0
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 512Mi

controls.why: the open CIDR is a variable default — iac-terraform.js resolves variables, so this one tests whether that resolution actually reaches the security-group rule
controls.control: Security groups must not allow unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to administrative ports

_hardenedMeansHardened: A `hardened` variant must be clean of EVERYTHING the engine checks, not just the control under test. Scoring is 'any finding on this file', deliberately — matching on the engine's own rule names would grade it against vocabulary it chose itself. The cost is that an unrelated true positive on the hardened variant reads as NO-FLIP. It happened once here: the hardened Dockerfile pinned its base by digest but still had no USER directive and still installed an unlicensed package, so two correct findings made a covered control look broken.
_headroom: Controls are added whenever the bench saturates. A gate that cannot fail measures nothing — this PRD's governing rule — and it hit 14/14 immediately after CloudFormation, Bicep and Helm support landed. The eight controls after docker-unpinned-base were added for that reason and deliberately reach past what was just built: host PID namespace, Linux capabilities, publicly-reachable managed databases, wildcard IAM in CloudFormation, Azure network rules, and ADD-from-URL.
_tiers: Controls carry an optional `tier`. Untiered ones are the direct shapes — a literal property with an unambiguous hardened opposite. `tier: "hard"` ones require something a regex cannot do: reasoning about what a set of actions adds up to, resolving a value through a parameter or variable, or noticing an ABSENCE. They are here so the bench keeps discriminating after the direct shapes are covered, and they are NOT expected to pass. Closing one should be a deliberate decision with its own design, not a wider pattern.
